scenes.visual: Title card 'Planting Past the Edge' over the SAND coastline from the first film, a headland with the dashed 'range edge' line. Reuses the first film's COLOUR MAP. COLOUR MAP (shared by both films, the take-homes and the lesson): niche box TEAL on axes 'temperature' (horizontal) and 'soil moisture' (vertical); coastline map in SAND with sea in pale blue; places where conditions fall inside the niche shaded TEAL on the map; places where the species is found = DARK GREEN dots; sink plants = GREY dots fed by BLUE immigrant arrows; lambda always written as the symbol λ; the dune plant = a small green rosette icon labelled 'the dune plant'; neighbouring plants = ORANGE tufts; cleared plots = bare tan soil; each plot's λ shown as a vertical bar with a dashed line at λ = 1. All numbers appear only as on-screen text. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: A plant's range ends at a headland. Why does it stop there? Is it the cold, the neighbours, or seeds never getting there?
scenes.visual: DARK GREEN dots run up the coast and stop at a headland. Three cards pop up beside it: a thermometer 'conditions', ORANGE tufts 'neighbours', a seed with a stop sign 'never arrived'.
scenes.narration: A plant's range ends at a headland. Why does it stop there? Is it the cold, the neighbours, or seeds never getting there?

scenes.tts: The first film drew a niche as the conditions where lambda stays at or above one without immigrants. Now we test an edge directly.
scenes.visual: A small inset replays the TEAL niche box labelled 'λ ≥ 1 without immigrants', then slides aside as the camera moves in on the headland.
scenes.narration: The first film drew a niche as the conditions where lambda stays at or above one without immigrants. Now we test an edge directly.

scenes.tts: Each answer is a different kind of limit. Conditions make an abiotic limit. Other species make a biotic limit. Never arriving makes a dispersal limit.
scenes.visual: The three cards relabel in turn: 'abiotic limit', 'biotic limit', 'dispersal limit', each lighting as it is named.
scenes.narration: Each answer is a different kind of limit. Conditions make an abiotic limit. Other species make a biotic limit. Never arriving makes a dispersal limit.

scenes.tts: The direct test is to plant the species beyond the edge and follow it for years. But plant the same way inside the range too. Transplanting itself is a shock, and a bad year can kill plants anywhere.
scenes.visual: Square plots appear: three inside the range, one at the edge, two beyond it, each sown with 'the dune plant' icons by the same gloved hand. The inside plots are labelled 'controls'.
scenes.narration: The direct test is to plant the species beyond the edge and follow it for years. But plant the same way inside the range too. Transplanting itself is a shock, and a bad year can kill plants anywhere.

scenes.tts: Then split every site in two. On randomly chosen plots, clear away the neighbouring plants. On the others, leave them.
scenes.visual: Each plot splits into two halves: one keeps ORANGE tufts ('neighbours left'), the other turns to bare tan soil ('neighbours cleared'). A small die icon labels the choice 'random'.
scenes.narration: Then split every site in two. On randomly chosen plots, clear away the neighbouring plants. On the others, leave them.

scenes.tts: Count survival, growth and seed production across the whole life cycle. From those, estimate lambda for every plot. One season's survival is not enough.
scenes.visual: Above each half-plot a vertical λ bar appears with a dashed line at λ = 1. Icons for 'survival', 'growth' and 'seed production' feed into each bar. A single 'first-year survival' icon alone is crossed out.
scenes.narration: Count survival, growth and seed production across the whole life cycle. From those, estimate lambda for every plot. One season's survival is not enough.

scenes.tts: First possible result. Lambda beyond the edge stays at or above one, with or without neighbours. The species can live there. Seeds have not arrived, or have not recolonised empty patches.
scenes.visual: All bars fill; the beyond-edge bars, in both halves, rise above the dashed line. Label: 'result 1: dispersal limit (likely)'. Bar heights schematic.
scenes.narration: First possible result. Lambda beyond the edge stays at or above one, with or without neighbours. The species can live there. Seeds have not arrived, or have not recolonised empty patches.

scenes.tts: The dune plant looks like this case, though its neighbours were never cleared. Planted beyond its northern edge, the population more than tripled in twelve to fourteen years.
scenes.visual: Caption 'Cross and Eckert'. The beyond-edge plot fills with dune plant icons over a counter '12 to 14 years'; label 'more than tripled'; small note 'neighbours not tested'.
scenes.narration: The dune plant looks like this case, though its neighbours were never cleared. Planted beyond its northern edge, the population more than tripled in twelve to fourteen years.

scenes.tts: Second result. Beyond the edge, lambda falls below one only on plots where neighbours remain. Cleared plots do fine. Other species are setting the limit.
scenes.visual: Bars reset and refill: beyond-edge 'neighbours left' bars drop below the dashed line; 'neighbours cleared' bars stay above it. Label: 'result 2: biotic limit'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Second result. Beyond the edge, lambda falls below one only on plots where neighbours remain. Cleared plots do fine. Other species are setting the limit.

scenes.tts: Third result. The plots inside the range grow. Beyond the edge, plots shrink whether or not neighbours were cleared. What does that implicate?
scenes.visual: Bars reset and refill: inside bars above the line; beyond-edge bars below the line in both halves. Question card: 'What is implicated?'
scenes.narration: Third result. The plots inside the range grow. Beyond the edge, plots shrink whether or not neighbours were cleared. What does that implicate?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The bars hold; a 5-second ring timer counts down.

scenes.tts: The conditions beyond the edge. Climate is a strong candidate. But herbivores, pathogens or missing soil partners need their own tests first.
scenes.visual: Label 'result 3: conditions beyond the edge'. The thermometer card glows with a tag 'candidate, not proved'; small icons of a grazer, a fungus spot and soil partners appear with 'test these too'.
scenes.narration: The conditions beyond the edge. Climate is a strong candidate. But herbivores, pathogens or missing soil partners need their own tests first.

scenes.tts: One more result. Every plot fails, inside the range as well as beyond it. Then the test cannot single out the edge. Handling, the seed or a bad year may be to blame. Check them, then repeat the study.
scenes.visual: All bars, inside included, drop below the dashed line. A storm cloud labelled 'bad year?' and a glove labelled 'handling?' appear. Banner: 'the edge cannot be singled out'. A circular arrow 'repeat'.
scenes.narration: One more result. Every plot fails, inside the range as well as beyond it. Then the test cannot single out the edge. Handling, the seed or a bad year may be to blame. Check them, then repeat the study.

scenes.tts: So here is the reading rule. Compare lambda beyond the edge with lambda inside the range, on plots with and without neighbours.
scenes.visual: A two-by-two table builds: columns 'inside' and 'beyond', rows 'neighbours left' and 'neighbours cleared', each cell a small λ bar.
scenes.narration: So here is the reading rule. Compare lambda beyond the edge with lambda inside the range, on plots with and without neighbours.

scenes.tts: That comparison separates access, neighbours and conditions beyond the edge. A map of where the species grows cannot do it on its own.
scenes.visual: The three limit cards ('access', 'neighbours', 'conditions') snap onto the table's patterns; small grazer, fungus and soil-partner icons sit outside the table marked 'need their own tests'. The plain occurrence map beside it is greyed with a label 'map alone: cannot tell'.
scenes.narration: That comparison separates access, neighbours and conditions beyond the edge. A map of where the species grows cannot do it on its own.

scenes.tts: Plant beyond the edge, with the same planting inside, and measure lambda. Where it replaces itself beyond the edge, the range stops short of the niche.
scenes.visual: The headland with its plots, bars and controls, shrinking under the spoken line.
scenes.narration: Plant beyond the edge, with the same planting inside, and measure lambda. Where it replaces itself beyond the edge, the range stops short of the niche.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Transplants with inside controls tell conditions, neighbours and access apart.'
